10 Best B.Com Project Ideas for Students

Deciding on a right project topic is one of the most important academic decisions a B.Com student will make. A good project improves your quality of work and demonstrates your analytical capabilities, abilities to research, and competencies of the business. It does not matter if you are a B.Com regular student or an online B.Com course from the best online universities in India , your project work is very much essential to exhibit your capability to learn and academic potential.

As more students opt for UGC approved online degree courses , selecting impactful commerce project topics is now more important than ever. To help you get started, here’s a curated list of the 10 best B.Com project ideas that are relevant, practical, and research-worthy.
How to Choose the Right B.Com Project Topic?
Before jumping into ideas, ask yourself:

items: What interests you the most—finance, marketing, banking, or social impact?
Do you have access to real data or research materials?
Is the topic aligned with your future career goals?
Can you add fresh insights to the topic using recent trends?

blocks.x: If you are studying through a UGC approved distance education university , be sure your topic matches the requirements of the academic requirements of their institution. Many online BCom degree programs provide mentoring sessions or project supervisors to help guide you during this phase.
10 Best B.Com Project Ideas
1. Digital Payment Systems and Their Effects on Consumer Behavior
Discuss how mobile wallets, UPI, and digital banking have modified purchasing habits and behaviors. Ideal for students interested in fintech, consumer behavior, or retail data analysis.
2. Impact of GST on Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMES)
Explore how the Goods & Services Tax affected SMEs pricing, tax compliance and general functioning.
3. SWOT of an Assumed Company
Choose a brand (Zomato, TCS, Paytm) or well-known company and evaluate its Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats. This can relate to brand, company, or category of business analysis.
4. Growth of E-commerce and Changing Consumer Preference
Explore how companies like Amazon and Flipkart have changed purchasing habits and behaviors – in particular after COVID.
5. Management of Working Capital Process in Manufacturing Companies
Explore the working capital cycle and how companies manage daily cash, cash flows, and inventory. Suitable for students mainly interested in finance.
6. Effect of Social Media Marketing on Business Growth
Evaluate how social media can bring brand awareness and lead generation for businesses through the use of platforms like Instagram, Facebook, or LinkedIn.
7. Comparative Study of Public and Private Sector Banks
Compare parameters like interest rates, customer satisfaction, digital banking features, and financial performance.
8. Financial Analysis of a Listed Company
Pick a company listed on NSE/BSE and evaluate its balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow to assess performance.
9. Investment Patterns and Awareness Among Young Investors
Study how Gen Z and millennials are investing—stocks, crypto, mutual funds—and their understanding of risk and returns.
10. Microfinance and Its Role in Women Empowerment
Explore how micro-lending platforms help rural women start businesses and become financially independent.
Key Tips for Scoring High in Your B.Com Project Work

items: Start early – Don’t wait until the last semester.
Pick a topic with available data – This makes analysis easier.
Include real-world examples – Add case studies or surveys.
Use visuals – Charts and graphs can strengthen your presentation.
Stick to format – Follow your university’s structure, even in online graduation courses .
Cite your sources – Academic integrity is essential.
Proofread and edit – Grammar and formatting matter.

The Growing Relevance of Project-Based Learning in Online B.Com Courses

As academic models develop, project-based learning has emerged as a dominant manner of delivery in commerce education in the setting of online B.Com courses offered by UGC approved distance education university . Traditionally, learners engaged in rote memorization, while project work effectively encourages students to experiment, investigate, develop, and apply concepts in real-world contexts.

For online universities in India , projects will most likely represent more than credits for their course, since they simulate real world business hurdles. Whether you’re analyzing the financials of a listed company or exploring the adoption of digital payments in rural India, your project helps bridge the gap between classroom theory and industry application.

In fact, many online graduation courses are now structured around online degree courses that mandate project work, presentations, and case study submissions. These components improve not just your resume, but also your soft skills—communication, critical thinking, problem-solving, and time management.
Using Your Project to Stand Out in a Competitive Job Market
With thousands of students graduating every year, what sets you apart in the eyes of employers? The answer often lies in your project.

Let’s say you’re applying for an internship at a fintech firm. If your final-year project is titled “Impact of UPI and Mobile Wallets on Consumer Spending in Tier 2 Cities”, you immediately position yourself as someone who has knowledge and interest in their domain. This creates relevance and gives you an edge over generic candidates.

If you’re pursuing your B.Com through an online degree courses India , you can leverage your flexibility to dig deeper into research. Some UGC approved online certificate courses also complement your project by helping you build technical skills like Excel modeling, Power BI dashboards, or financial forecasting tools.
Research Resources for Online B.Com Students
One of the most common challenges students face—especially those in online BCom degree programs—is finding quality research data. Here are some reliable sources you can explore:

items: RBI Database – Great for banking and finance topics
NITI Aayog & Government Reports – Excellent for economic or SME-related studies
Annual Reports of Companies – For financial analysis and SWOT reports
Statista & McKinsey Insights – Ideal for industry-specific data
Google Scholar & ResearchGate – For peer-reviewed academic papers
Survey Tools (Google Forms, Typeform) – For collecting primary data

FAQs
1. What are the eligibility criteria for doing a B.Com project?

Typically, you need to be in your final year of a B.Com program—either regular or through an online university in India —to undertake a project. Some institutions may require prior coursework in research methodology.
2. How do I choose the best B.Com project topic for my interests and career goals?
Choose a topic that intersects your personal interest, career direction, and availability of resources. If you’re interested in finance, topics like investment analysis or working capital are ideal.
3. What is the ideal structure or format for a B.Com project report?
Most universities follow a format that includes:

items: Title page
Certificate and acknowledgment
Introduction
Objectives
Research methodology
Data analysis
Findings & conclusion
Bibliography

blocks.x: Always check with your institution or LMS portal if you’re pursuing an online B.Com course .
4. Can I do a B.Com project on a company, industry, or topic of my own choice?
Yes. As long as the topic is relevant to your course and approved by your project guide or academic advisor, you can choose your own subject.
5. Where can I find reliable sources and data for my B.Com project research?
Use:

items: Company annual reports
Government portals (like RBI, MCA)
Market research platforms (Statista, PwC, Deloitte)
Academic journals and e-books from UGC approved online certificate courses
